title: Shakshuka
description: Shakshuka is a traditional Arabic-inspired dish of eggs gently poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce. It is rich, aromatic, and commonly served for breakfast or brunch with warm bread for dipping.

ingredients.title: For the Sauce
items: 1 can (400g) chopped tomatoes or 5 fresh ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped
½ cup vegetable or chicken stock
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.title: For the Eggs
items: Crumbled feta cheese or soft goat cheese (optional)
Extra parsley or cilantro for garnish
Drizzle of olive oil for serving

ingredients.title: Optional Extras
items: Toasted pita or crusty bread for serving

instruction.title: Method
steps:
1. Prepare the Base:
• Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
• Sauté onions for 3–4 minutes until soft.
• Add bell peppers and cook 5 minutes until tender.
• Add garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.

2. Build the Flavors:
• Add cumin, paprika, coriander, turmeric, and chili flakes; toast 1 minute.
• Stir in tomato paste and cook 1–2 minutes.
• Add tomatoes and stock, season with salt, pepper, and sugar.
• Simmer 10–15 minutes until thick but still saucy.

3. Finish the Sauce:
• Stir in half the parsley and cilantro.
• Adjust seasoning and create small wells for eggs.

4. Cook the Eggs:
• Crack eggs into wells.
• Cover and cook 5–8 minutes until whites are set and yolks are soft.
• Alternatively, bake at 180°C (350°F) for 5 minutes.

5. Plate and Serve:
• Garnish with remaining herbs and cheese.
• Drizzle olive oil and add optional za’atar or harissa.
• Serve with warm bread or pita.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve with toasted pita or crusty bread
Pair with feta cheese and olives
Enjoy as a breakfast, brunch, or light dinner
Add harissa for extra heat and depth

chefTips: Use ripe tomatoes for the best natural sweetness.
Do not overcook peppers; slight texture adds character.
Toast spices in oil to deepen flavor complexity.
Keep yolks slightly runny for best presentation and taste.
Generous fresh herbs brighten and balance the dish.
